meta.title: NIST AI RMF for GenAI
meta.thesis: NIST AI RMF for GenAI is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A company needs a repeatable risk process for generative AI systems from design to monitoring. By the end, they should be able to build or review NIST AI RMF GenAI risk register mapped to govern, map, measure, and manage, measure identified risks tied to owners and controls, and catch the failure where risk work becomes a one-time checklist instead of a lifecycle practice.

mentalMap.title: NIST AI RMF for GenAI: mental map
mentalMap.caption: Use Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage to turn GenAI risk into owned evidence and controls.
mentalMap.oneLineThesis: The NIST AI RMF helps teams run a repeatable risk loop for GenAI systems: govern the process, map the context, measure risks, and manage controls.

modules.title: Govern: make risk ownership real
modules.sub: Name authority, policies, reviewers, and evidence before risk work begins.
modules.summary: Govern creates the organizational machinery that makes GenAI safety repeatable instead of heroic.
objectives: Define who can approve, block, and revisit GenAI releases.
Connect governance to policies, evidence, and incidents.
Explain why model-only safety review is too narrow.

blocks.title: Govern is the operating system for risk

spans.text: Problem anchor: a lesson-generation agent cites sources, drafts modules, stores traces, and can call tools. A prompt change improves fluency but increases unsupported claims. Without governance, everyone agrees it is concerning and nobody owns the release decision.

The Govern function names roles, risk appetite, policy stack, review cadence, escalation path, and evidence requirements. For GenAI, this includes content policy, privacy policy, tool-use policy, evaluation policy, vendor review, incident response, and change management.

items.text: Product framing: governance decides which risks are acceptable for this use case.
Engineering framing: governance becomes gates, logs, evals, approvals, and rollback switches.
Review framing: governance gives reviewers authority, not just advisory comments.

blocks.title: Worked artifact: GenAI risk owner map

spans.text: Feature: automated lesson enrichment. Owner: learning product lead. Safety reviewer: trust and safety. Security reviewer: platform. Data owner: KB curator. Block authority: release manager when evals or data review fail. Evidence: risk register, eval report, source-citation audit, prompt version, model route, trace sampling plan, and incident playbook.
This is intentionally mundane. RMF value comes from making risk work durable enough that the next prompt, model, retrieval, or tool change reruns the right checks.

blocks.title: Govern function
blocks.prompt: What does Govern add that a one-time eval report does not?

options.text: A guarantee that no model will fail.
Owners, authority, policy, review cadence, and evidence expectations for future changes.
A replacement for privacy and security review.

blocks.explanation: Govern makes the process repeatable and accountable; it does not eliminate risk.

modules.title: Map: describe the system in its real context
modules.sub: Identify users, data flows, tools, vendors, harms, misuse, and impacted groups.
modules.summary: Map turns a broad GenAI feature into a concrete risk surface with boundaries and assumptions.
objectives: Map the use case, users, data, tools, and deployment context.
Name foreseeable misuse and affected groups.
Identify risk sources outside the model.

spans.text: A GenAI system is not just a model endpoint. It includes prompts, retrieval sources, memory, user interface, tool permissions, logs, analytics, vendors, reviewers, and users who may misunderstand generated output. Mapping makes those pieces visible before measurement.

For a learning studio, mapped harms include unsupported teaching claims, biased feedback, privacy leakage, unsafe advice, prompt injection through sources, overreliance by learners, and tool actions outside the educational role.

blocks.title: Map dimensions for a lesson agent

cells.text: Who uses it and what decisions could follow?
learner age range, teacher role, product copy, escalation path
What sensitive or copyrighted material can enter?
data inventory, retention table, redaction policy
Can the system act, publish, email, browse, or mutate data?

blocks.title: Case study: the risk was in retrieval, not the model

spans.text: A source note in the KB contains outdated legal language. The model faithfully summarizes it, cites it, and the lesson becomes wrong. A model-only map misses this; a system map includes source freshness, provenance, retrieval filters, citation checks, and curator ownership.

modules.title: Measure: test risks with evidence
modules.sub: Use evals, red-team cases, slice checks, privacy review, and trace sampling.
modules.summary: Measure converts mapped risks into evidence about likelihood, severity, control effectiveness, and gaps.
objectives: Separate offline evals from production monitoring.
Explain why red-team examples must match the mapped context.

spans.text: If the risk is hallucinated citations, measure citation faithfulness and unsupported-claim rate. If the risk is prompt injection from KB notes, test poisoned source chunks. If the risk is privacy leakage, inspect logs, traces, redaction, and vendor data settings. Generic chat quality scores are not enough.

Measurement includes offline evals, adversarial examples, human review, slice checks, telemetry, incident reports, and post-launch monitoring. The evidence should say what the control caught and what it missed.

Risk: lesson agent invents sources. Test set: 80 prompts across RAG, safety, and infra categories with known KB sources. Metrics: citation coverage, unsupported-claim rate, source freshness, render validation, and reviewer rejection. Red-team set: poisoned notes instructing the model to ignore citations. Pass rule: no critical unsupported claims and citation coverage above the release threshold by category.

blocks.ruleOfThumb: Measure the failure mode you mapped, not the metric that is easiest to compute.
blocks.useWhen: Use a mixed evidence plan when GenAI risks span factuality, privacy, injection, safety, and user reliance.
blocks.avoidWhen: Avoid passing release based only on a small happy-path demo or an average quality score.

modules.sub: Tie mitigations to owners, rollout decisions, monitoring, and incident response.

blocks.title: Risk register gate check
blocks.code:
risk = {
    "id": "GENAI-CITE-01",
    "harm": "unsupported source claim in lesson",
    "owner": "learning-quality",
    "severity": "high",
    "controls": ["citation_eval", "source_provenance", "human_review"],
    "evidence": {"unsupported_claim_rate": 0.01, "critical_failures": 0},
    "residual_risk_accepted_by": "release-manager",
}
assert risk["owner"]
assert risk["controls"]
assert risk["evidence"]["critical_failures"] == 0
assert risk["residual_risk_accepted_by"]

spans.text: This sketch checks the release discipline: a risk must have an owner, controls, evidence, and residual-risk acceptance before promotion.

predictThenReveal.prompt: What is missing if the register has controls but no owner?
predictThenReveal.answer: No one is accountable for maintaining, reviewing, or changing those controls after release.

spans.text: Check that an AI-generated RMF plan uses Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage as functions, not decorative headings. It should name system context, risks, owners, evals, controls, residual risk, monitoring, and update triggers for model, prompt, KB, route, or tool changes.

items.text: Does each risk link to evidence rather than vague concern?
Does each control have an owner and review cadence?
Does the plan say what blocks release?
Does it include incident learning and change management?

blocks.title: Residual risk

options.text: A risk that can be ignored because a model passed one eval.
The risk that remains after controls, evidence, and mitigations are applied.

blocks.explanation: Managing risk includes deciding what remains and who accepts it.

objectives: Write a retrieval prompt for RMF risk work.

blocks.title: Retrieval prompt for the whole lesson

spans.text: Answer this from memory: "How do I apply NIST AI RMF to a GenAI feature?" Include Govern roles, Map context and misuse, Measure evals and monitoring, Manage controls and residual risk, then update after incidents or system changes.
Spaced recall: module 2 mapped retrieval and tools as part of the system. The final register must update when those non-model pieces change.

blocks.ruleOfThumb: Use the RMF as an operating loop, not a launch poster.
blocks.useWhen: Use it when a GenAI feature is user-facing, retrieval-grounded, tool-using, safety-sensitive, or costly to get wrong.
blocks.avoidWhen: Avoid RMF paperwork that is disconnected from code, evals, release gates, monitoring, and incidents.

spans.text: Pick a GenAI feature. Write one row with risk, affected users, severity, likelihood, context, measurement, controls, owner, residual risk, release gate, monitoring signal, and update trigger. Then explain which RMF function each field supports.

hallucination.label: Hallucination
hallucination.laymanDefinition: A generated output that appears plausible but is unsupported or false.
hallucination.technicalNote: NIST GenAI risk work treats confabulation as one risk to measure and manage, especially where users may rely on generated claims.

prompt_injection.label: Prompt injection
prompt_injection.laymanDefinition: A manipulation attempt that turns untrusted text into model instructions.
prompt_injection.technicalNote: Prompt injection belongs in the RMF risk register when retrieval, tools, or external content can change system behavior.

guardrail.label: Guardrail
guardrail.laymanDefinition: A control chosen to reduce a named GenAI risk.
guardrail.technicalNote: In RMF work, guardrails must be tied to mapped risks, measured evidence, owners, and review cadence.

privacy.label: Privacy
privacy.laymanDefinition: The governance of personal and sensitive data across prompts, logs, traces, vendors, and outputs.
privacy.technicalNote: Privacy is mapped as context, measured through data-flow review, and managed through minimization, redaction, access, retention, and vendor controls.

owasp.label: OWASP
owasp.laymanDefinition: A practical security lens for LLM application risks.
owasp.technicalNote: OWASP controls can support the RMF Manage function for prompt injection, excessive agency, and sensitive information disclosure.

risk_register.label: Risk register
risk_register.laymanDefinition: The working table of risks, context, measurements, controls, owners, and residual risk.
risk_register.technicalNote: For GenAI, the register should cover hallucination, harmful content, data leakage, injection, tool misuse, monitoring, and incident response.
